channel.title: Bay Area Sports Blog
channel.description: Every Bay Area team, argued about properly. The 49ers, Warriors, Giants, A's and Sharks, written by a fan, not a network.

item.title: The A's Have Five Hitters on the IL and deGrom One Hit What Was Left
item.description: Rangers 8, Athletics 1. deGrom allowed one hit over seven, Gage Jump gave up seven earned, and the five best bats in the organization are all hurt at once.

item.title: Giants 7, Braves 3, and This Team Has Quietly Been Fun for a Week
item.description: Devers opened it with his 30th, Molina went five with six strikeouts and no walks, and a four run sixth buried Atlanta. Five wins in the last eight.

item.title: Rafael Devers Hit Number 30 in Atlanta and I Would Like Some Apologies
item.description: Devers got to 30 homers in the first inning against Atlanta. Only the second Giant to do it since Bonds in 2004, on a 57 win team, after a summer of being called soft.

item.title: Eldridge Goes 4 for 5 With 4 RBI and the Giants Are Fun Again
item.description: Giants 7, Diamondbacks 2 in the nightcap. Bryce Eldridge matched career highs with four hits and four RBI, the first Giants rookie to do it since Posey in 2010.

item.title: They Ran Ron Wotus at the Lineup Card. The Game Hadn't Started Yet.
item.description: Ron Wotus got ejected during the lineup card exchange before Game 1 of the doubleheader against Arizona. Not in the third. Not in the ninth. Before the first pitch.

item.title: Vitello Got Run Again, and This Time He Took Logan Webb With Him
item.description: Two days after the six run ninth, Tony Vitello got thrown out in the third inning against Arizona, and Logan Webb got tossed with him. Five ejections. Fifty five wins.

item.title: 49ers 18, Raiders 12: A Kicker Won a Football Game
item.description: 49ers 18, Raiders 12 in the preseason finale. Eddy Pineiro went 6-for-6 including a 59 yarder and the defense allowed no touchdowns.

item.title: Bryce Eldridge Is Back, and Buddy Kennedy Is the One Who Paid for It
item.description: The Giants activated Bryce Eldridge off the bereavement list Thursday and designated Buddy Kennedy for assignment to make room. Eldridge is hitting .252 with 14 homers. Kennedy hit .121 in 33 at bats here.

item.title: Fire Tony Vitello. The Bullpen Is the Whole Case.
item.description: Reds 10, Giants 9 after a six run ninth. Twenty four saves in forty four chances. Same organization that had the fourth best bullpen in baseball last year. Enough.

item.title: Giants Blew a Six Run Lead in the Ninth and It Isn't Even Over
item.description: Nine to three going to the ninth. Then Eugenio Suarez hit a grand slam, the same Suarez Vitello got ejected screaming about in the first. I'm done with this season.

item.title: Bryce Eldridge on the Bereavement List: Take the Week, Kid
item.description: The Giants put Bryce Eldridge on the bereavement list on Monday. Nobody's said why and nobody has to. He'll be away about a week, and every other thing about this season can wait.

item.title: Rafael Devers Hit His 29th Homer and Nobody Said a Word
item.description: Devers went deep again Wednesday, three straight games, 29 homers on a 54-78 team. He gets called soft and not a winning player and I do not buy a second of it.

item.title: Vitello Ejected in the First Inning on a Check Swing
item.description: Tony Vitello got tossed in the top of the first on Wednesday for yelling get it right at a check swing call on Eugenio Suarez. Fourth ejection of his rookie year as a manager, and honestly, good.

item.title: The Warriors Spent All Summer Chasing a Star and Signed Georges Niang
item.description: Golden State's big summer ended with a 33-year-old corner shooter coming off a lost year. One year, $3.9 million, the fifteenth roster spot, and the second apron.

item.title: Jed York Arrested in Ohio: Two Misdemeanors and Nothing From the 49ers
item.description: 49ers owner Jed York was arrested Sunday morning in East Palestine, Ohio, pleaded no contest Monday to disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools, and the team has said nothing.

item.title: Mike Evans and Brock Purdy: The Receiver He Has Never Had
item.description: Mike Evans lines up for the 49ers this year, and Brock Purdy has never thrown to a receiver built like this. Here is why that pairing has Niner Nation buzzing.

item.title: Purdy and Warner Were Talking Trash in Practice, and It Was Beautiful
item.description: Warner won a rep and talked. Purdy threw right over his head to Deebo and screamed it back at him. Then they laughed about it. Practice 16 in Santa Clara wasn't a walkthrough.

item.title: Twins 9, Athletics 6: Rally Falls Short
item.description: Twins 9, Athletics 6 at Sutter Health Park: Jeffrey Springs took his twelfth loss, Minnesota piled up sixteen hits and led 9-1, and a four run ninth got the A's within three. 51 and 81.

item.title: Giants 5, Reds 0: Shutout at Oracle
item.description: Giants 5, Reds 0 at Oracle Park: San Francisco scored twice in the first, Rafael Devers hit his 27th for three more in the second, and six pitchers combined on a five hit shutout. 53 and 78.

item.title: A's 7, Astros 6: Down Six, Somehow Alive
item.description: Athletics 7, Astros 6 in Houston: down 6-0 after four, Brian Serven's three run homer started a six run fifth, and Max Muncy's solo shot in the seventh won it. They are 51-80.

item.title: Red Sox 5, Giants 4: Swept at Fenway
item.description: Red Sox 5, Giants 4 at Fenway Park: San Francisco led three to nothing before Matt Wilkinson allowed four runs in the fourth, Boston finished a sweep, and the Giants fall to 52 and 78.

item.title: A's 4, Astros 3: Win Number Fifty, on a Wild Pitch
item.description: Athletics 4, Astros 3 in Houston: Jacob Lopez struck out nine in six innings, Luis Medina handed the lead back, and a wild pitch and a ground out won it in the eighth. They are 50-80.

item.title: Red Sox 3, Giants 2: Vitello Blew Another Ninth Inning
item.description: Red Sox 3, Giants 2 at Fenway Park: San Francisco carried a two nothing lead into the ninth, Tony Vitello burned through Dylan Smith and Sam Hentges, and Wilyer Abreu walked it off. They are 52-77.

item.title: 49ers 41, Chargers 17: The Best Night of the Summer
item.description: 49ers 41, Chargers 17 at SoFi: Jacob Cowing took a punt 83 yards, the run game piled up 146, and San Francisco led Harbaugh's Chargers 20 to 3 at the half.

item.title: Royals 6, A's 2: Swept in Four, and Seventeen of Twenty One
item.description: Royals 6, Athletics 2: Bobby Witt Jr. homered and scored three, Gage Jump gave up five runs in four innings, and Kansas City finished off a four game sweep.

item.title: Guardians 5, Giants 2: Eleven Strikeouts, Series Won Anyway
item.description: Guardians 5, Giants 2: Gavin Williams struck out eleven, Willy Adames hit a 418 foot two run homer, and San Francisco still left Cleveland with the series.

item.title: Raiders 22, Texans 20: The No. 1 Pick Threw a Pick Six
item.description: Raiders 22, Texans 20: Fernando Mendoza threw a pick six on his third pass and Aidan O'Connell snuck one in from a yard out with fourteen seconds left.

item.title: Royals 9, Athletics 7: A Seven Run Eighth Buried Them
item.description: Royals 9, Athletics 7: the A's led 5-1 in the eighth in Kansas City and the Royals scored seven. Second blown late lead in two nights. 49-78.

item.title: Giants 1, Guardians 0: One Run Was Enough for Once
item.description: Giants 1, Guardians 0: Houser and Dylan Smith threw seven scoreless in Cleveland, a Bericoto ground ball scored the only run, and Messick struck out ten in a loss.

item.title: Royals 4, A's 3: A Two Run Ninth Inning Lead, Gone in Ten Minutes
item.description: Royals 4, Athletics 3 at Kauffman Stadium: the A's led 3-1 into the ninth, Hogan Harris gave up three, Bobby Witt Jr. walked it off, and the A's fall to 49-77.

item.title: Barry Bonds and the Giants: The Years, the Numbers, the Argument
item.description: Barry Bonds played fifteen seasons for the Giants and hit 586 of his 762 home runs here. The 73 home run year, the 2002 World Series, and the argument.

item.title: Cal Football Schedule 2026: Every Game, Date, Time and TV
item.description: The full Cal Golden Bears 2026 football schedule: every game, date, kickoff time and TV network, from the UCLA opener to the Big Game on 21 November.

item.title: Cal Basketball Schedule 2026-27: Every Game Announced
item.description: The Cal basketball schedule for 2026-27: the announced non conference games, every ACC opponent home and away, and the 2025-26 results for reference.

item.title: Guardians 8, Giants 1: Eldridge Homered, Nothing Else Happened
item.description: Guardians 8, Giants 1 in Cleveland: Bryce Eldridge homered for his 14th, Jo Adell drove in six, and one run was the entire Giants offense. They are 51-74.

item.title: Josuar Gonzalez Is the Best Giants Prospect in a Generation
item.description: Josuar Gonzalez is 18, a switch-hitting shortstop ranked as high as seventh in baseball, and he is hitting .339 at Low-A San Jose. Why Giants fans should care.

item.title: San Jose Sharks Playoff History: Every Run, Year by Year
item.description: The complete San Jose Sharks playoff history: all 21 postseason trips, the 1994 upset, the 2016 Stanley Cup Final, the 2019 comeback and the drought since.

item.title: Warriors Projected Rotation 2026-27: Who Actually Plays
item.description: Our projected Warriors rotation for 2026-27: the ten men who play, the minutes each should get, who closes, and what changes when Jimmy Butler is back.

item.title: Warriors Depth Chart 2026-27: Every Position, Explained
item.description: The Warriors depth chart for 2026-27: the projected starters, the bench behind them, where Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody fit, and where this roster runs out.

item.title: When Were the San Jose Sharks Founded? The Full Origin Story
item.description: The San Jose Sharks were founded on 9 May 1990 and began play in 1991-92. The Gund brothers, the North Stars swap, the Cow Palace years and how they got the name.

item.title: They Took Brandon Aiyuk's Locker Out. That Is How You Know It Is Over.
item.description: Brandon Aiyuk's locker stall is gone from the 49ers locker room. It survived all of last season after he left the team. Now the standoff is basically over.
